label: early original token right after a 2 (esp. in sequences starting t/g)
explanation: Sparse feature (about 0.03% of steps). 99.5% of its mass is in the original phase at t=2-4, and it fires almost only when the digit 2 was input one step back (75% of mass) or two steps back (91% of mass for either). It essentially never fires at t<2, at t>=5, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Activations are largest when the first token is t or g (or 2) and the prefix is X 2 2: the top examples are all t 2 2 [i], g 2 2 [i] and similar. Predicate coverage goes up across activation quartiles (0.30 to 0.66). Letters such as i, x, l and k as the current input make firing more likely. The context condition is necessary but far from sufficient: most steps that match it do not activate, so precision stays low (best dev F1 about 0.24), and some exact combination of prefix and current token that I could not capture decides whether it fires.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev2_tok=2 (+5.42), prev_tok=2 (+4.05), prev_tok=1 (+4.00), orig0=t (+3.92), t=2 & prev_tok=2 (+3.72), orig0=g (+3.32). Lower it: in_tok=n (-2.21), in_tok=z (-2.12), orig_idx=-1 (-1.98), in_tok=g (-1.84).
